notes: Only scan 084, its assigned two witnesses, and its supplied notation table were read for this assignment. No other scan or reader output was inspected. No OCR, recognition tool, or external research was used. The full image was viewed once, and each full-resolution half once. All running words and mathematical tokens, including agreed readings, were compared against the image.

Line count 23 consists of 19 main-text/display baselines, three slanted annotation lines, and the separate bottom foliation 83. The overwritten E occupies its existing formula baseline; it is not an additional line. There is no author page number written at the top.

Seventeen unique crops were made with Pillow LANCZOS to 2200 pixels wide, autocontrast, and light sharpening. The characteristic-zero note was rotated clockwise 28 degrees. No place was recropped. Each crop is linked by its original pixel box.

The old symbol under E_K is genuinely a replacement state. Its left vertical and top bar survive, but its possible right leg is entangled with the live E. The extra C doubt π|Γ is retained in the draft and unresolved list, not added to marks, which is limited to the supplied M1232.

The characteristic-zero note stands immediately beside (8) and applies to its Kummer/inertia identification. It is a side annotation, with no deletion or insertion leader. Its hyp has no abbreviation point, while car. has a clear one.

The first connector in (7) is a plain shaft, while the following three have right arrowheads. The source’s lack of a comma after the final 1 is preserved. The tilde is placed on every x shown in I and N; the bars over k(x) and K and the external stars in (8) are retained.

The last two lines are readable. They stop at des factorisations; no ensuing factorization or punctuation is written on this leaf. H’s statement about a missing intervening page is editorial prose and is not transcribed or adopted as an archival conclusion.

The lower short stroke under O in U’s subscript is preserved as an underline. The spacing le dit favors two written groups; its confidence remains medium because ordinary pen lifts can also separate parts of one lexical unit.

M1232 remains undecided after review of the existing crop: donc is preferred, but the first stroke’s d bowl and the compressed low letters are not independently complete enough to rule out sur. No new crop was made. The supplied diff row for the alternative alone is classified as uncertainty markup rather than a substantive first-reading difference.

Blind review of (7) exposes a small isolated point above the numerator x. Its role as a deliberate diacritic rather than an incidental ink point is not secure; the text now retains x/dotted-x uncertainty locally, without placing the entire formula in doubt. The initial connector remains a plain shaft and the following connectors arrows. All eight token-different boxes were inspected; the short form hyp has no supplied stop, and le dit remains two written groups.

check_events.outcome: Defining I_x-tilde as the kernel of the displayed map N_x-tilde → Gal(overline k(x)/k(x)) gives exactness at N. The source also asserts surjectivity at the Galois group; this leaf alone does not supply the preceding local setup needed to prove that assertion, so no stronger verification is claimed.

For the standard henselian discrete-valuation setting with residue characteristic zero, all ramification is tame and the inertia description uses the inverse system of roots of unity. This is compatible with the two T_infinity expressions in (8) and the author’s explicit characteristic-zero annotation. No positive-characteristic extension of the assertion is inferred.

For an integral divisor D of finite type over Q, the residue field at its generic point is its function field and is finitely generated over Q. This checks the algebra of the paragraph under the stated/assumed finite-type setup; it does not add a new hypothesis to the manuscript text.

If the kernel of E_K → E_S is the closed normal subgroup generated by the inertia groups I_x-tilde, a continuous homomorphism to a profinite target kills that kernel exactly when it kills every generating inertia group. Its kernel is closed and normal, so vanishing on the generators implies vanishing on their closed normal closure. The page’s factorization criterion is therefore consistent with its stated generation assertion.
